summary.headline: Ramkrishna Forgings Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 28% YoY to Rs 1,216.78 crore, with EBITDA margin at 17.1%, and management guides to further improvement in FY27.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was Rs 1,216.78 crore, up 28% YoY and 11% QoQ, with EBITDA excluding other income of Rs 208.19 crore (up 111% YoY, 27% QoQ) and margin of 17.1%. Profit before tax was Rs 64.33 crore, held back by about Rs 10.4 crore of consolidation effects (Rs 5.9 crore subsidiary profit elimination and Rs 4.5 crore Mexico subsidiary loss). FY26 consolidated revenue was Rs 4,238 crore (up 5%) and EBITDA Rs 642.70 crore (up 15%), while PBT fell 24% to Rs 112.58 crore versus Rs 148.79 crore (excluding exceptional items) in FY25. Q4 orders won totalled Rs 594 crore over four years, split 56% automotive and 44% non-automotive.

segments.name: Forgings
segments.commentary: Forging utilisation about 70% in Q4 FY26 versus 83% in Q4 FY25, per the analyst's reading of the presentation; management attributes the gap partly to the 8,000-ton press line added. Cold forging utilisation is about 40%, held back by slow global PV approvals; management hopes for 75-80% by FY26 year-end (FY27 per the call's context).

segments.name: Castings
segments.commentary: Capacity is 62,000 tons (cited as 78,000 tons by one analyst, with about 70,000 tons referenced by management); production was 26,000 tons in FY26 and sales are lower due to machining mix. Management expects 85-90% utilisation over the year and margins of about 15-16%, with Rs 400-500 crore of incremental revenue from the new March-end capacity.

segments.name: Aluminium forgings
segments.commentary: Post commissioning, bulk supplies have started to EV equipment makers globally; management cites margins of about 14-15%, with commodity realisation near Rs 400/kg.

segments.name: Railway wheelsets (JV)
segments.commentary: Rail wheel JV expected to start production by Q1 FY27, with 230,000-wheel capacity and a railway offtake guarantee of about 40,000 wheels in FY27 for revenue of roughly Rs 400-450 crore.

segments.name: Trailer axles
segments.commentary: Revenue of about Rs 120 crore in FY26; management targets about Rs 250 crore in FY27 and a 10% market share.

guidance_outlook: Revenue: no FY27 number given; management expects 'healthy growth' on current order book and capacity. Analyst cited a prior 10-15% CAGR upper limit for FY27-28, and management declined to confirm it.
EBITDA margin: management expects continued improvement, with 100-150 bps better margin at around 80% utilisation if energy price increases are passed on.
Utilisation: overall capacity utilisation targeted at about 80% in FY27, roughly 350,000 tons of forging and casting; press plant around 85% by FY27 year-end.
Debt: reduction of at least Rs 400-500 crore in FY27, supported by promoter funding and operating performance.
Capex: FY27 capex limited to about Rs 400 crore at most, mainly JV contribution (about Rs 50 crore still to be paid) and value-add; no FY28 capex frozen yet.
Export mix: management expects exports to rise above 40% of volumes within about two years (from a historical 40:60 export:domestic split), with exports more remunerative.
Titanium/stainless aerospace alloys: order book reflection expected by FY26 year-end, but revenue not expected before FY29.
capex_capacity: Rail wheel JV: commercial production to start immediately after commissioning, around end-May/June 2026; 300 trial wheels to be submitted in June/July 2026.
Forging press line: 8,000-ton press added; press plant utilisation targeted at about 85% by FY27 year-end.
Casting: about 62,000-ton capacity, 26,000 tons produced in FY26; new capacity added by end-March 2026 is expected to generate Rs 400-500 crore of revenue in coming years.
Standalone casting business began commercial production on 31 March 2026, so nil standalone revenue in FY26.
Ring rolling running at 121% utilisation; no plans to add ring rolling capacity in FY27.
demand_pricing: North America Class 8 demand is strong; destocking in North American warehouses over the last three months, with fresh revenue expected from Q1 FY27; management expects this to last to about Q3 CY27.

Q4 orders of Rs 594 crore (four-year program): Rs 334 crore auto (Rs 323 crore CV, of which more than 50% export; Rs 11 crore EV) and Rs 258 crore energy (energy storage, North America) plus Rs 2 crore off-highway.

Pricing is pass-through: steel is passed on quarterly with a one-quarter lag; gas and other consumables are negotiated yearly. Management is seeking compensation for geopolitical energy cost increases via force majeure, with talks at an advanced stage.

Realisation: management attributed the lower realisation versus Q4 FY25 to lower raw material prices and cited a better product mix in H2 FY26; the analyst cited export realisation rising from Rs 1.77 lakh to Rs 1.85 lakh per ton.
Shipping costs up 15-20% and transit times up 15-20 days; floating inventory said to be in line. No West Asia revenue or exposure.
Domestic auto demand was strong after the September GST rate cut, with M&HCV, tractors and PVs reporting double-digit wholesale growth in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Rs 1,550 crore FY27 order book include castings, and what casting volumes and revenue are expected?
qa_highlights.answer: The figure covers forgings and castings together. Management expects 85-90% casting utilisation over the year, with margins of about 15-16% and Rs 400-500 crore of additional revenue. Management declined to put a figure on the incremental revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 debt and capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt is to be reduced by at least Rs 400-500 crore in FY27. Capex is capped at about Rs 400 crore, mostly JV equity and value-add, with about Rs 50 crore of JV equity still to be paid.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for margins and revenue growth in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No revenue number was given, but management expects healthy growth. The EBITDA margin should keep improving, and at about 80% utilisation it could be 100-150 bps above the Q4 level if energy cost increases are passed on.

qa_highlights.question: How much did trailer axles contribute, and what are the targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue was about Rs 120 crore in FY26 at a 4-5% market share. The FY27 target is about Rs 250 crore at about 10% share.

qa_highlights.question: What is the wheelset JV's contribution and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Production starts by Q1 FY27 and about 40,000 wheels are expected in FY27 under the railway offtake guarantee, for revenue of roughly Rs 400-450 crore. Pricing is still being reset for two years of inflation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timing for aerospace/titanium revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Orders should start reflecting in the order book by FY26 year-end, but revenue is not expected before FY29 given 12-24 month lead times and approvals.

risks_watch: Energy and gas cost pass-through: consumables are not automatically passed on, and the compensation claim from customers is still under negotiation.
Cold forging utilisation at about 40% depends on slow PV approvals in global markets.
Rs 400-500 crore debt reduction target depends on promoter funding and operating performance.
Geopolitical and Middle East conflict risks, plus freight costs up 15-20% and transit times up 15-20 days.
Rail wheel JV start-up: 300 trial wheel approvals due June/July 2026; 40,000-wheel FY27 delivery commitment.
Mexico subsidiary loss (Rs 4.5 crore in Q4) and consolidation eliminations (Rs 5.9 crore) weighed on PBT.
Rs 42 crore ECL provision on receivables booked in Q4, linked to electricity duty income recognised as exceptional income.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes, utilisation and margins; cautious on timing, with repeated refusals to give quarterly or FY27 revenue numbers. Management was most vague on energy cost pass-through and product approvals.

So we are not looking anything in terms of our revenue before FY29.

adds.what: Casting capacity added by end-March 2026 (standalone casting began commercial production 31 Mar 2026), expected Rs 400-500 cr incremental revenue

growth.why: Management gives no quantified FY27 revenue number, only 'healthy growth' on the current order book, but backs it with specific items: a 230,000-wheel JV with a ~40,000-wheel offtake (Rs 400-450 cr), casting capacity adding Rs 400-500 cr revenue, trailer axles targeted to double to Rs 250 cr, and utilisation rising to ~80% from about 70%.
